target.name: Dyna Robotics
target.founder: Lindon Gao, York Yang, Jason Ma

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $120M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Dyna Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $120M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private peers and 1 public company across the robotics sector, including Series B-stage companies like Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B), as well as earlier-stage benchmarks.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $120M raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A-to-next-stage progression, implying a valuation of $240M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector comparables—Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics—yields a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $2.0B.

The triangulated analysis produces a low-to-high range of $204M to $2.0B, with a median of $970M. The wide spread reflects methodological tension: stage-progression suggests a more conservative $240M floor based on capital deployed, while peer comparables suggest substantially higher valuations typical for later-stage peers. Key uncertainties include the applicability of Series B peer multiples to an early Series A company and the degree to which Dyna's specific progress, traction, or market position justifies positioning at or below the peer median versus the upper quartile of comparable valuations.
